premises.text: Parents leave hospital anxious about SIDS and breathing crises, while current baby monitors are outdated and do not actually show whether the baby is breathing
premises.evidence_span: the current monitors on the market stink. They're old, they're outdated, and they don't actually tell you if your baby is breathing or not

premises.text: Owlet smart sock uses clinical-style pulse-ox tech in a flexible waterproof form to send heart rate, oxygen, temperature, rollover, and sleep alerts to a parent's phone
premises.evidence_span: It's a smart sock that sends heart rate and oxygen levels to a parent's smartphone and can alert you in case of an emergency

premises.text: Multi-sensor pulse-ox design (four sensors, nine combinations) keeps accurate wireless readings as an infant's foot triples in size
premises.evidence_span: With four sensors, we're getting nine different combinations, and we're getting a great reading the whole time

premises.text: Sock-generated infant vitals will build the largest infant health dataset to enable predictions from common cold to life-threatening conditions
premises.evidence_span: creating the largest data set of infant health data that's ever been known

value.text: Empower parents and improve infant health by alerting on emergencies and keeping parenting fulfilling rather than fear-driven
value.evidence_span: empower parents and it's gonna improve the health of infants all over the world

causal_links.evidence_span: anything that saves a baby's life is worth it
alert you in case of an emergency
predictions from anything from the common cold to things that are more life-threatening
